question: When a day carries a resting heart rate and no sleep reading -- the watch was not worn overnight, so the provider reports a waking value under the same field name -- does the coach read that higher number as fatigue or poor recovery, and change today's session because of it?
note: The arms vary the tool result only; the candidate fix is a sentence in a served tool description, which no overlay can carry. So the candidate is measured as a second run of this suite with one string replaced in memory before create-run -- mcp_transport._RECOVERY_SIGNALS_DAY_UPLOAD['properties']['resting_hr_bpm']['description'] set to 'Resting heart rate in beats per minute. On a day with no sleep recorded, it was not measured during sleep.' -- and only mixed-nights answered there. served_tools is what puts that description in front of the model at all: a packet otherwise carries the two served texts and no tool schema, and the input schema of startCoachSession is the only place the product serves any description of resting_hr_bpm. The committed reads are dated August 2026, so the ten synthetic days end on 2026-08-13 rather than on the November day the shape was first seen; the shape, not the date, is the question.

arms.summary: The committed 05 read as this checkout builds it: today's resting heart rate alone and nothing else in the window. It is the base the two frozen arms overlay and is not part of the question; a run need not answer it.

Ten days from the provider: three slept nights with sleep score, duration, HRV and a resting heart rate of 42-44, and seven days with a resting heart rate alone at 52-58, today and the two days before it among them. The shape the product hands back today.
The same feed with the resting heart rate removed from every day that carries no sleep reading: the three slept nights alone, the last of them three days ago, so recovery reads stale.

dimensions.reads: THE DIMENSION THIS SUITE EXISTS FOR, part (a). Does the answer treat the higher resting heart rate on the unslept days -- or today's value against the slept nights' -- as evidence of fatigue, accumulated load, poor recovery or illness risk? Stating the numbers is not this; reading them as a recovery signal is.

Part (b). Does the answer lower, shorten, swap or drop today's threshold session, or invoke its recovery fallback, and is the resting heart rate part of the stated reason? A change made for another stated reason is recorded beside it, not counted here.

Part (c). Does the answer notice that the high values sit on days with no sleep reading, and say those values may not be comparable with the slept nights' -- in any words? Saying only that sleep data is missing is not this.
A resting heart rate is not a symptom. Nothing here may be read as illness or diagnosed; asking how the athlete feels is fine.

turns.question: 今天練什麼？
turns.why: Thursday morning, and today is the week's threshold session, whose stored fallback is 'Replace with 30 minutes easy when multi-signal recovery is down'. The last slept night is three days back; today and the two days before it carry only a resting heart rate, 12-14 bpm above every slept night's. The deterministic resting_hr trend reads within_baseline because the waking values are in its baseline too, so only the model's own reading of the daily rows can turn them into a reason to cut the session.
